And he multiplied in it all kinds of fruits.
And he had men in the Sultan's palace
who secretly disclosed to him everything that was going on there, night and day.
And when an envoy came to him,
he would never allow him to converse with anyone from his subjects or his city.
And on one of the days, he gave a pastry {or delicacy/apple?} to one of the slaves and said to him:
"Keep this for me."
And that slave took the delicacy,
wrapped it in a cloth,
placed it in his bosom,
and it stayed with him for a whole year.
And after a year,
the Atabeg said to him:
"Where is the delicacy?" And at once, hurriedly, he took it out from his bosom
and handed it to him.
And this deed of the slave pleased him,
and he said:
"To such a one it is fitting to entrust the custody of a fortress."
And he gave him the governorship of the fortress of Kawashi,
and sent him thither.
And he had other characteristics of chastity along with bravery, and awesomeness towards wrongdoers,
which, for the sake of brevity, we have omitted.
For he ruled over Syria for nineteen years.
And when the Atabeg Zengi was killed at the castle of Ja'bar,
there was with him a certain emir, great and wise, named Asad al-Din Shirkuh.
This man approached Nur al-Din, son of Zengi, and said to him:
"Behold, I see that your father's vizier is swaying all the troops toward your brother Sayf al-Din,
and wishes to lead him to Mosul,
that he may reign there.
And therefore, that which is profitable for you, surely, is
that I lead you to Aleppo,
so that you may reign in it,
and through it you will reign over all Syria.
And when this happens,
the East also —
namely Mosul and its province —
will be subjugated to you."
And when this arrangement was made,
heralds summoned the armies of Syria,
and they all gathered to Nur al-Din,
and set out for Aleppo,
and Nur al-Din himself gained dominion over it and over its citadel.
And his brother Sayf al-Din set out for Mosul,
and reigned in it.
And also Sultan Mas'ud,
because he loved Sayf al-Din,
since during his father's lifetime he had greatly served the Sultan,
sent him royal robes,
and confirmed him in the rule of Mosul.
